title: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)

content.caseIdentity: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
content.facts: A Constitution Bench considered the duration and scope of protection granted under Section 438 CrPC after anticipatory bail is granted.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether anticipatory-bail protection must be limited to a fixed period and whether it ordinarily ends when the accused is summoned or charges are framed.
content.ratioDecidendi: Protection under Section 438 CrPC should not invariably be limited to a fixed period; ordinarily, anticipatory bail can continue through the trial, subject to appropriate conditions and case-specific reasons for limiting its duration.
content.holding: Confirmed that protection granted under Section 438 CrPC does not invariably end upon the filing of chargesheet or framing of charges; it can normally continue till the conclusion of the trial.
content.relevance: Duration of anticipatory bail and absence of automatic expiry.

sources.evidenceNote: Official Supreme Court judgment identifies Sushila Aggarwal as the five-Judge Constitution Bench reference and reproduces the answers that anticipatory-bail protection should not invariably be time-limited and ordinarily can continue until trial.
Official Supreme Court office report confirms the case identity and proceeding record for Sushila Aggarwal and others v. State (NCT of Delhi).
